descriptions: Websites whose main product or offering is an AI/ML system: chatbots and assistants, AI agents, LLM apps and APIs, generative AI for text, images, video, audio or code, model hosting, prompt libraries, vector databases, MLOps, and AI tool directories. Signals: 'AI-powered', 'GPT', 'LLM', 'generate with AI', 'train your model'. Assign here only when AI is the core value proposition; if AI is just a feature of a product in another domain (e.g. an accounting app with AI insights), use that domain's category instead.

Websites that serve software developers and engineering teams: IDEs and code editors, APIs and SDKs, CLIs, libraries and frameworks, testing, debugging, monitoring, Git and code review, CI/CD, DevOps, cloud hosting and deployment, databases, backend services, and developer documentation. Signals: 'API', 'SDK', 'open source', 'deploy', 'documentation', code snippets. Coding assistants that are primarily AI products may fit AI & Machine Learning; choose here when the tool is a general developer utility or platform.

Websites offering B2B software or services for running a company: operations, HR and payroll, project and team management, customer support, business intelligence, ERP, logistics, procurement, consulting, agencies, and outsourcing. Signals: 'for teams', 'enterprise', 'streamline operations', 'request a demo'. Use a narrower category when one clearly applies (Marketing & Sales, Finance, Legal & Compliance, Jobs & Careers, Productivity).

Websites for personal or team efficiency: note-taking, task and to-do managers, calendars and scheduling, knowledge bases, time tracking, focus and habit tools, personal workflow automation, browser extensions, file organization, and email or meeting helpers. Signals: 'get organized', 'save time', 'manage tasks', 'automate your workflow'. Company-wide operations or project management suites lean toward Business.

Websites that help businesses attract, convert, and retain customers: SEO, advertising, social media management, email marketing, CRM, sales outreach, lead generation, landing pages, growth analytics, affiliate and influencer marketing, and brand management. Signals: 'grow your audience', 'generate leads', 'increase conversions', 'campaigns'. Marketing agencies and marketing blogs also belong here.

Websites about money: banking, fintech, payments and payment processing, investing and trading, cryptocurrency, accounting, bookkeeping, invoicing, budgeting, personal finance, insurance, loans, taxes, and financial news or data. Signals: 'invest', 'payments', 'portfolio', 'budget', 'APR', 'accounting'. Use when handling, tracking, or moving money is the core function; online stores that merely accept payments belong in E-commerce & Shopping.

Websites where people buy goods or that support online selling: online stores and brands selling physical or digital products, marketplaces, storefront builders, dropshipping, price comparison, coupons and deals, product reviews, and order or inventory tools. Signals: 'add to cart', 'shop now', 'free shipping', 'sell online'. A store's category is usually E-commerce even if its products relate to another topic, unless the site is mainly editorial or informational about that topic.

Websites whose purpose is teaching or learning: online courses, learning platforms, tutoring, language learning, test prep, flashcards and study tools, homework help, school and university sites, kids' educational content, and teacher resources. Signals: 'learn', 'course', 'lesson', 'curriculum', 'students', 'certification'. Corporate training tools count here; job-search or career-coaching sites belong to Jobs & Careers.

Websites about physical or mental wellbeing: workouts and fitness tracking, yoga, meditation, mental health, sleep, nutrition and calorie tracking, telehealth, medical information, clinics and health providers, supplements, and wellness. Signals: 'workout', 'symptoms', 'therapy', 'healthy', 'wellness'. Competitive sports content belongs in Sports; recipes and restaurants belong in Food & Drink.

Websites about everyday personal life that fit no narrower category: hobbies and crafts, home and garden, DIY, parenting and family, pets, dating and relationships, fashion and beauty, weddings, personal development, astrology, and general lifestyle blogs. Signals: 'home decor', 'parenting tips', 'self-improvement', 'hobby'. Prefer a specific category (Food, Travel, Health, Design) when the topic clearly matches.

Websites for planning or booking trips: flights, hotels, vacation rentals, tours and activities, itineraries, destination guides, travel blogs, maps and navigation for travelers, visa and currency tools, and tourism boards. Signals: 'book a trip', 'destinations', 'things to do', 'check-in', 'itinerary'. Restaurants and food content go to Food & Drink; car-focused sites go to Automotive.

Websites where food or drink is the central subject: recipes and cooking, meal planning, restaurants and reservations, food delivery, grocery, food and beverage brands, wine, coffee, cocktails, and food blogs. Signals: 'recipe', 'menu', 'ingredients', 'order food', 'brew'. Calorie counting and diet-health tracking belong in Health & Fitness.

Websites for casual leisure and pop culture: movies, TV shows, streaming, celebrity news, trivia and quizzes, memes and humor, fan sites, event and ticket listings, and fun or novelty sites. Signals: 'watch', 'stream', 'trailer', 'celebrity', 'funny'. Playable games go to Games, music to Music & Audio, and serious news to Media & Publishing.

Websites whose value comes from people interacting: social networks, messaging and chat apps, forums and discussion boards, community platforms, groups and meetups, networking sites, and creator-fan communities. Signals: 'join the community', 'connect with', 'members', 'followers', 'discussion'. Sites that only publish content for readers belong in Media & Publishing.

Websites that publish information for readers or listeners: news outlets, magazines, blogs, newsletters, journals, podcasts publications, online publications, and content aggregators. Signals: 'latest news', 'subscribe', 'articles', 'editorial', bylines and publication dates. Tools that help people create content go to Content Creation; a blog about a specific niche may fit that niche's category instead if it is the site's clear focus.

Websites for visual and creative work: UI/UX and prototyping tools, graphic design, logo makers, illustration, photography and photo editing, video editing, animation, 3D modeling, mockups, fonts, icons, stock assets, portfolios, and design inspiration. Signals: 'design', 'templates', 'edit photos', 'portfolio', 'mockup', 'render'. Writing, blogging, and podcasting tools belong in Content Creation.

Websites that help people produce and publish content: writing assistants, blogging platforms, newsletter builders, podcast production, creator tools for YouTubers and streamers, caption and thumbnail generators, content schedulers, and creator monetization. Signals: 'create content', 'for creators', 'publish', 'grow your channel'. Visual design tools go to Design & Creative; sites that are the published content itself go to Media & Publishing.

Websites centered on sound: music streaming and discovery, artist and band sites, music creation and DAWs, instruments and music lessons, audio editing, sound effects and samples, text-to-speech and voice tools, and audio hardware. Signals: 'listen', 'tracks', 'mix', 'beats', 'audio', 'instrument'. Podcast production tools may fit Content Creation.

Websites where games are played, discussed, or made: video games, mobile and browser games, indie games, puzzles, game engines, mods, game guides and databases, esports, and game development assets. Signals: 'play now', 'levels', 'multiplayer', 'walkthrough', 'game dev'. Casual quizzes and trivia belong in Entertainment.

Websites whose main purpose is protecting people or systems: cybersecurity, password managers, authentication and identity, VPNs, encryption, antivirus, threat detection, privacy tools, breach monitoring, and secure communication. Signals: 'protect', 'encrypt', 'zero trust', 'vulnerability', 'anonymous', 'secure login'. Use when protection is the core value, not a side feature.

Websites about property: listings and search, home buying and selling, rentals, mortgages and home valuation, property management, real-estate agents and brokerages, and real-estate investing. Signals: 'for sale', 'for rent', 'listings', 'square feet', 'realtor'. Home decor and DIY belong in Lifestyle.

Websites that connect people with work or support careers: job boards, recruiting and applicant tracking, resume and cover-letter builders, interview prep, freelance marketplaces, career coaching, salary data, and professional development. Signals: 'apply now', 'hiring', 'resume', 'careers', 'freelance'. A company's own careers page is not enough; classify by what the company does.

Websites about law and regulation: law firms and lawyer directories, legal services, contract drafting and review, e-signature, intellectual property, policy generators, legal research, and regulatory compliance such as GDPR, HIPAA, and SOC 2. Signals: 'attorney', 'contract', 'terms', 'compliance', 'legal advice'. A standard legal notice or privacy policy on an unrelated site does not make it a Legal site.

Websites related to public institutions and civic life: government agencies and services, elections and voting, political information and advocacy, public records and open data, policy tracking, permits and municipal services, and citizen engagement tools. Signals: '.gov', 'citizens', 'election', 'legislation', 'public services'. Charities and fundraising go to Nonprofit & Social Impact.

Websites of or for mission-driven organizations: nonprofits and charities, donation and fundraising platforms, volunteering, cause-based crowdfunding, sustainability and climate initiatives, humanitarian aid, and social-good projects. Signals: 'donate', 'our mission', 'volunteer', 'make an impact'. Political parties and government agencies go to Government & Civic.

Websites about physical devices and their software: consumer electronics, smart home, wearables, robotics, drones, sensors, 3D printers, embedded systems, maker projects (Arduino, Raspberry Pi), and IoT platforms. Signals: 'device', 'firmware', 'sensor', 'smart', 'specs', 'connect via Bluetooth'. Vehicles belong in Automotive; online stores selling gadgets belong in E-commerce & Shopping.

Websites for scientific and academic work: research databases and paper search, academic journals and preprints, lab software, scientific data and simulations, citation managers, and content on biology, physics, chemistry, space, and other sciences. Signals: 'study', 'peer-reviewed', 'dataset', 'experiment', 'researchers'. General education and courses belong in Education.

Websites about competitive sports: live scores and statistics, teams and leagues, fantasy sports, sports news, training and coaching for athletes, sports betting information, and athlete or fan communities. Signals: 'scores', 'standings', 'season', 'league', 'match'. General exercise and gym content belongs in Health & Fitness.

Websites where vehicles are the central subject: cars, motorcycles, EVs and charging, car buying and selling, maintenance and repair, car reviews, fleet management, and automotive technology. Signals: 'dealership', 'horsepower', 'EV', 'repair', 'test drive'. Ride-hailing and travel planning belong in Travel.

Fallback for websites that genuinely fit none of the other categories after considering all of them. Use only as a last resort. Do not use for sites that are merely ambiguous, parked domains with no content, or sites that fit two categories; pick the closest match instead.
